name: Grimes Grave Goddess

attributes.attribute: small white chalk figure from Grimes Graves, Norfolk
found at flint mines aged about 4000 BCE
buried with chalk tools and antler offerings

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Grimes Grave Goddess is a small British deity whose figure came from Norfolk in England. Miners there dug pits up to 50 feet deep using only deer antlers as shovels in a site from about 4000 BCE. Carved from white chalk, the squat and smirking figure may show a pregnant woman and recalls the Sheela na Gig. People hid the figure with a chalk phallus, chalk balls, a chalk lamp, and antlers. Her true name and meaning are lost.

okr.objective: Tell of the tiny chalk Grimes Grave Goddess and the offerings that share her pit.
key_results: Miners dug 50-foot pits with deer antlers at Grimes Graves.
The squat figure, roughly carved from chalk, may be pregnant.
Her original name and meaning remain unknown.
